source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A community that can identify its own problems, agree on priorities and act together to solve them shows:
questions.rationale: Community competence is the ability to collaborate in identifying needs, reach consensus on goals, agree on means and act together; it is linked to empowerment.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Community competence (PDF p. 224)
questions.quote: Community competence is defined as the ability of the community to (a) collaborate effectively in identifying its problems and needs

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Unlike health education, community organizing aims mainly to:
questions.rationale: Community organizing builds group problem-solving and decision-making so people act collectively for self-reliant development.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Community organizing (PDF p. 231)
questions.quote: the nurse's efforts are directed towards organizing and mobilizing the people to initiate and sustain changes as a group or as an organization.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Area selection, community profiling, and entry and integration with the people belong to which phase of community organizing?
questions.rationale: The preparatory phase includes area selection, profiling, entry and integration.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Community organizing phases (PDF p. 231)
questions.quote: Preparatory Phase. The acüvifies in the preparatory. phase include area selection, community profiling, entry in the community and integation with the people.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: During integration with a poor community, the nurse should:
options: Choose a modest dwelling people will visit
questions.rationale: Integration guidelines: adapt the community's lifestyle, choose a modest dwelling, avoid raising expectations, join social activities.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Integration (PDF p. 232)
questions.quote: Choose a modest dwelling which the people, especially the economically disadvantaged will not hesitate to enter.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which guideline should a nurse follow when entering a new community for organizing work?
options: Stay only in the health center
questions.rationale: The nurse is clear about objectives and limitations, recognizes local authorities and seeks people where they gather.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Integration (PDF p. 232)
questions.quote: Avoid raising expectations of the people. Be clear with your objectives and limitations.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: The most important quality the nurse looks for when spotting potential community leaders is:
questions.rationale: Leaders need not be educated or affluent; they should understand community problems, have people's trust and be willing to work for change.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Organizational phase (PDF p. 232)
questions.quote: one important consideration in selecting potential leaders will be their willingness to work for the desired change.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Forming a core group of potential leaders from different sectors happens in which phase of community organizing?
questions.rationale: The organizational phase includes social preparation, spotting leaders, core group formation and setting up the organization.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Organizational phase (PDF p. 232)
questions.quote: Organizational Phase. The organizational phase consists of activities leading to the formation of a people's organization.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: The community diagnosis and the training of community health workers are done in which COPAR phase?
questions.rationale: The education and training phase strengthens the organization through community diagnosis, CHW training, health services and leadership training.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Education and training phase (PDF p. 233)
questions.quote: This can be achieved by conducting the community diagnosis, training of community health workers, undertakng health services and mobilization and leadership SHIIS baining.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Who decides which residents will be trained as community health workers?
questions.rationale: After the community diagnosis, the community decides CHW roles and selects trainees based on agreed criteria.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Training of CHWs (PDF p. 233)
questions.quote: Based on an agreed upon criteria, the people will decide who will be trained as community health workers

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Before designing training for barangay health workers, the nurse gives them a pre-test and a skills test. This step is the:
questions.rationale: The TNA estimates trainees' entry competencies and guides the training curriculum.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Competency-based training (PDF p. 235)
questions.quote: This is done by giving them a pre-test to evaluate their level of knowledge and attitude and readiness

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: As the people's organization becomes able to manage its own health programs, the nurse gradually turns over work. This is the:
questions.rationale: In phase-out, the nurse prepares for turnover and follow-up until full disengagement.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Phase-out (PDF p. 234)
questions.quote: the nurse gradually prepares for turn-over of work and develops a plan for monitoring and subsequent follow-up

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: The community organization links with NGOs and government agencies to get resources it cannot provide itself. This is the:
questions.rationale: As the organization grows, resources are sourced through collaboration with other organizations, facilitated by the nurse.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Intersectoral collaboration (PDF p. 234)
questions.quote: Assistance and support in any form can be funneled into the organization through collaboration with other organizations and communities.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In community health nursing, supervision of midwives and health workers is best seen as:
questions.rationale: Supervision is developmental and enabling, aimed to remedy rather than punish poor performance; in CHN it is mainly coaching.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Supervision (PDF p. 239)
questions.quote: In community health nursing, supervision is seen more as a coaching (Gillies 1989) function rather than a function ofcontrol.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: What is the first step in making a supervisory plan for midwives?
questions.rationale: Steps: analyze supervisory needs, prioritize, set objectives, select strategies and resources, identify evaluation indicators.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Supervisory plan (PDF p. 240)
questions.quote: The nurse conducts a situational analysis focusing on supervisory needs assessment.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: At the closing part of a supervisory visit, the PHN should:
questions.rationale: The visit has an opening, body and closure; closure expresses appreciation and plans the next visit with the worker.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Supervisory visit (PDF p. 241)
questions.quote: Closure — The nurse expresses appreciation and support extended during the visit. Together with the worker, she plans for the subsequent visit.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Population Groups
questions.stem: A PHN plans care for all 60 hypertensive clients in her catchment area as a group. This is:
questions.rationale: Caseload management addresses common problems of an aggregate in a program; case management is directed to individual clients.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Caseload management (PDF p. 242)
questions.quote: Caseload management differs from case management because it focuses on the common problems of aggregates or groups.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In program planning, which statement is a goal rather than an objective?
options: Reduce child malnutrition in the barangay
Mothers will give complementary food at 6 months
80% of mothers will attend 4 feeding classes
questions.rationale: A goal is a broad desired end addressing the health problem; objectives are specific and measurable.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 8 Goal and objective setting (PDF p. 213)
questions.quote: It is generally broad and not constrained by time or resources. It states the ultimate desired state. Objectives are more precise.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: In the PRECEDE model, a mother's belief that measles vaccine causes fever is a(n):
questions.rationale: Predisposing factors are knowledge, beliefs and attitudes; enabling are resources and access; reinforcing are rewards and social pressures.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 8 Situational analysis (PDF p. 209)
questions.quote: Which of the behaviors are due to predisposing factors (beliefs, attitudes and knowledge)?

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: Mothers do not bring children for vaccination because the health station is a 3-hour walk away. In the PRECEDE model, this is a(n):
questions.rationale: Enabling factors relate to the immediate environment, accessibility to resources and services.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 8 Situational analysis (PDF p. 209)
questions.quote: Which are due to enabling factors (influences of the immediate environment, accessibility to resources and services)?

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: A youth stops smoking after his barkada praises him and his parents reward him. These are:
questions.rationale: Reinforcing factors are rewards, punishments or feedback following a behavior, including social pressure.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 7 Causality and association (PDF p. 192)
questions.quote: Reinforcing factor — any reward or punishment or any feedback following or anticipated as a consequence of health behavior

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which three approaches does the book identify as needed for sustainable community health development?
questions.rationale: Sustainable development uses community-based (empowering), integrated and comprehensive (root-cause) approaches.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 9 Community organizing (PDF p. 230)
questions.quote: Community-based approach which empowers the people to address their health needs and problems
